advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test asserting every required_status_checks context in main-protection.snapshot.json for the optionality workflow matches an actual job `name:` in _optionality.yml (and that removed check names are absent).
evidence: The new tests anchor only on the job KEY `_OPTIONALITY_LOOP_JOB = "optional-extras"` (test file line 29), never on the job display `name:` that becomes the snapshot check context.
Workflow job display name that must match the snapshot: `.github/workflows/_optionality.yml:144` `name: optional extras isolate (per-extra venvs + union)`.
Snapshot required check context updated to that string but untested: `infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json:1` `{"context":"optional extras isolate (per-extra venvs + union)"}`.

rollback-mirror-lock.sh:83-84 POSTs the snapshot rules verbatim: `jq '{name, target, enforcement, conditions, rules, bypass_actors}' "${SNAPSHOT}" | api -X POST "/repos/${OWNER}/${REPO}/rulesets"` — a context with no matching job name would freeze main on rollback.
ABSENCE: `search_files` for `.snapshot.json` under tests/ returns only the comment reference at test_ci_workflow_parity.py:178; no test reads or asserts the snapshot's contexts.
advisory.finding: No test guards the parity the change exists to protect: that every check context in infra/github/main-protection.snapshot.json's required_status_checks matches an actual workflow job display name. rollback-mirror-lock.sh POSTs this list back verbatim on emergency rollback, so a stale context freezes main by requiring a check that never reports. The diff renamed the workflow job name AND edited the snapshot to match, but nothing asserts they stay in sync.
advisory.suggested_fix: Parse main-protection.snapshot.json's required_status_checks contexts and assert the optionality-related context equals the `optional-extras` job's `name:` from _optionality.yml; also assert the removed contexts (`extra "agents" installs`, `union [agents,eval,tracing] resolves`, etc.) are no longer present.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend the loop-shape test to assert the run text contains the absolute `"$v/bin/python"` (and `"$v/bin/rebar-mcp"`) invocations, the `rebar-mcp --help` mcp boot check, and the `extra_installed` probe.
evidence: test_optionality_loop_aggregates_failures_and_never_activates asserts only `rc=0/rc=1/continue/exit $rc` present and `activate` absent (lines 201-213); it does not assert `"$v/bin/python"` / `"$v/bin/rebar-mcp"` absolute-path usage.

Ticket AC: `- [ ] Every interpreter/console-script call in the loop uses an absolute "$v/bin/..." path` and `- [ ] rebar-mcp --help runs for the mcp iteration only, invoked by absolute venv path` — behaviors present in the workflow (_optionality.yml run body) but unguarded by the diff's tests.

test_optionality_loop_covers_every_declared_extra asserts only that labels appear in the `specs=` list (lines 224-239); it does not assert the loop retains `extra_installed` or the `rebar-mcp --help` invocation.
advisory.finding: The venv-loop tests do not assert the absolute `"$v/bin/..."` invocation rule that the ticket names as a silent-failure footgun — only `activate`-absence is checked. A regression to a bare `python`/`rebar-mcp` call (ambient interpreter, which can pass while testing nothing) would not be caught, nor would loss of the per-iteration `rebar-mcp --help` boot check or the `_optional.extra_installed()` probe.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_optionality_loop_aggregates_failures_and_never_activates, add assertions that the run text contains `"$v/bin/python"`, `"$v/bin/rebar-mcp"`, `--help`, and `extra_installed`, so a regression to a bare console-script call or a dropped boot/probe check reddens.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide whether reviewbot/ui/pricing/jira-datacenter/grounding-t2 need an install lane in the optional-extras loop (or document why they are intentionally excluded), since they currently get zero install-resolution CI.
evidence: src/rebar/_optional.py:34-48: `EXTRAS` = {agents, eval, tracing, grounding, metrics} only
_optionality.yml:188-196: specs cover agents,eval,tracing,grounding,metrics,mcp,union — reviewbot/ui/pricing/jira-datacenter/grounding-t2 have no install lane
tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:227: `missing = set(_optional.EXTRAS) - labels` — coverage guard is scoped to EXTRAS + {mcp,union}, so the un-probed extras are unguarded
advisory.finding: Shipped optional-dependency extras `reviewbot`, `ui`, `pricing`, `jira-datacenter`, and `grounding-t2` install real dependency stacks (fastapi/uvicorn/boto3, genai-prices, jira, pyright) but are neither in `_optional.EXTRAS` nor added to the loop's `specs`, so a broken/missing dependency declaration in any of them ships with zero install-or-resolution CI. The parity test only enforces `_optional.EXTRAS` keys plus `mcp`/`union`.
scenarios: A dependency floor typo in the `reviewbot` extra (e.g. an unpublished fastapi pin) lands green and only breaks when a consumer runs `pip install nava-rebar[reviewbot]`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that cross-checks every required_status_checks context in main-protection.snapshot.json against the actual rendered job/check names in the workflows, so any renamed check re-staleifying the rollback snapshot fails CI.
evidence: main-protection.snapshot.json: `"strict_required_status_checks_policy":true` with contexts `lint + type-check`, `pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.11)`, ... `eval discipline (offline — no model)`

infra/github/rollback-mirror-lock.sh:83-84: `jq '{name,target,enforcement,conditions,rules,bypass_actors}' "${SNAPSHOT}" | api -X POST .../rulesets` — the snapshot's required_status_checks are POSTed back verbatim on rollback

tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py:216-239: coverage/loop guards only cross-check the optional-extras job vs `_optional.EXTRAS`; no guard cross-checks the snapshot's full context list against the workflows' rendered job names
advisory.finding: The rollback snapshot's OTHER required_status_checks contexts (`lint + type-check`, the `pytest (...)` matrix cells, `import-linter (...)`, `clean core wheel (...)`, `eval discipline (offline — no model)`) are hand-maintained in `main-protection.snapshot.json` with no test asserting they still match live job check-context names; only the optional-extras job name is indirectly guarded. A rename of any of those jobs re-staleifies the snapshot, and since `strict_required_status_checks_policy:true`, an emergency rollback would demand a nonexistent check and freeze main.
scenarios: A later change renames the `pytest (ubuntu-latest, py3.12)` job or the `eval discipline` job; the snapshot is not updated; a subsequent `rollback-mirror-lock.sh` POSTs a ruleset requiring a check context that no workflow ever reports, blocking every merge to main.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Broaden the loop-label regex in test_ci_workflow_parity.py to accept digits/hyphens (or derive labels by splitting the specs list) so the coverage guard cannot silently miss a digit/hyphen extra name.
evidence: pyproject.toml:168-173: extras `jira-datacenter` and `grounding-t2` contain a hyphen/digit — outside the `[a-z_]+` class the guard matches
src/rebar/_optional.py:34: `EXTRAS: dict[str, tuple[str, str]]` — nothing constrains future keys to `[a-z_]` only
dropped.finding: The coverage-parity guard extracts loop labels with `re.finditer(r'"([a-z_]+):([a-z_,]+)"', run)`, whose `[a-z_]+` label class cannot match an extra name containing a digit or hyphen (e.g. a future EXTRAS key like `grounding-t2`). Such a key would be silently absent from `labels`, and if it were also absent from `specs` the `missing` set could still be computed against a name the regex can never see — weakening the very guard that is supposed to make a newly declared extra fail loudly.
scenarios: A future extra `grounding-t2` (or any digit/hyphen name) is added to `_optional.EXTRAS`; if the `specs` entry uses the hyphenated name the regex fails to capture it, and the coverage guard's set arithmetic no longer reliably proves the extra is present in the loop.
